item.title: Inflation eases in July as gasoline and grocery prices fall
item.description: Consumer prices in July were up 3.4% from a year ago — a smaller annual increase than in May or June. The news makes it less likely the Fed will feel the need to raise interest rates in September.
item.content:encoded:
Consumer prices in July were up 3.4% from a year ago — a smaller annual increase than in May or June. The news makes it less likely the Fed will feel the need to raise interest rates in September.

(Image credit: Justin Sullivan)

item.title: Greetings from a surreal expanse of sand dunes dotted with freshwater lagoons in Brazil
item.description: The pristine white sand dunes of the Lençóis Maranhenses National Park are bordered by thick jungle on one side and the Atlantic Ocean on the other. Thousands of lagoons fill up after the rainy season.

item.title: His wedding guests gave $6k to fund a health startup. Now it's won a $3 million prize
item.description: Dr. Raj Panjabi founded Last Mile Health to bring healthcare to people living in remote areas. The group is the 2026 recipient of the Conrad N. Hilton Humanitarian Prize.

item.title: Zhu Rongji, who drove China's 1990s economic reforms, has died at 97
item.description: Zhu was renowned for reforms that sought to transition China from the post-Maoist years to a more global market-oriented financial system, without ceding party control over the economy.
item.content:encoded: Zhu was renowned for reforms that sought to transition China from the post-Maoist years to a more global market-oriented financial system, without ceding party control over the economy.

item.title: Andrew Tate's extradition fight tests his influence with Trump's America
item.description: After President Trump took office, Andrew Tate proclaimed, "The Tates will be free." A year later, Tate is being held in federal prison after he was arrested following a U.K. extradition request.

item.title: Feel so busy you don't even realize you're busy? Try doing a time audit
item.description: The exercise can help you identify what's wasting your time — and make room for what matters, says psychotherapist Niro Feliciano. Take a moment to try it. You might be surprised with what you find.
